key_insight: The paper introduces a universal diffuse-interface surfactant framework that handles insoluble, soluble, and partially soluble cases in two-phase flows while preserving conservation, Galilean invariance, and reduction consistency.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more general and physically consistent way to model surfactant-driven Marangoni effects in multiphase CFD across different phase-field methods and solubility regimes.
method: General three-scalar non-equilibrium transport model for bulk and interfacial surfactant concentrations
Thermochemical-equilibrium reduction to two one-scalar models for common solubility scenarios
Coupling to Navier-Stokes via surface-tension forcing with Marangoni stress
evidence_signal: The framework is validated with 1D analytical transport tests, 2D advection-diffusion convergence studies, and fully coupled drop-in-shear simulations spanning insoluble, soluble, and partially soluble cases.
watch_item: The framework is theoretically general, but practical performance will depend on accurate parameterization and numerical robustness when coupling surfactant transport to interfacial flow dynamics.
paper_title: A universal diffuse interface modeling framework for surfactants
